name: Music, art and dance schools

problems.words: Make-up class requests are endless and we can't track who's owed what
quick_ideas: Write one make-up rule and share it with parents, so requests are judged the same way
List the make-ups owed today, so you have a starting point.

workzap_build.text: A lesson ledger that tracks missed and make-up lessons under your rules, with parents booking make-ups themselves.

problems.ask_first: Do make-up requests come mostly from illness, or from travel and exams?
problems.free_stops: How the rules and booking work is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many make-up requests are still unsettled at this week's end, so you see how big the backlog really is.
Keep one paper list of make-up lessons owed in the office, so every teacher checks the same place before promising a slot.

problems.words: Lesson packs expire but nobody checks
quick_ideas: Check every active pack's lessons used and expiry once, so you know where you stand
Tell families their pack status before renewing, so expiry isn't a surprise.

workzap_build.text: Packs and terms tracked with lessons used and expiry, with renewal reminders sent automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do packs expire mostly with lessons unused, or after the last lesson is taken?
problems.free_stops: The reminder timing is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many active lesson packs are already past expiry but still being used, so missed checks stop slipping by unnoticed.
Give one staff member a fixed weekly pack expiry check, so renewals are raised before lessons continue by accident.

problems.words: Trial lessons don't turn into enrolments
quick_ideas: List this month's trials and who joined, so you see the gap
Make one person follow up after every trial, so none are forgotten.

workzap_build.text: Every trial tracked to enrolment, with automatic follow-up reminders and conversion by discipline.

problems.ask_first: Do trials fail to convert in one discipline, or across all of them?
problems.free_stops: The follow-up timing is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare trial attendance by discipline against enrolments from those trials this month, so you see which classes sell themselves and which do not.
Give one teacher the job of recording each trial outcome that day, so follow-up stops getting lost after busy classes.

quick_ideas: Count who stayed from last term by discipline, so you see where the drop is
Ask leaving families for their one main reason, so you know what to fix.

workzap_build.text: Retention tracked by term and discipline as counts, with next-term reminders sent automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do children quit mostly after exams or recitals, or at any point in the term?
problems.free_stops: The retention reports and reminders are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare term-to-term returns for music, art and dance separately, so you spot where children are leaving fastest.
Keep one leaving-reason page at reception, so staff note the main cause each time a family stops classes.

problems.words: Weekday rooms are empty, Saturdays are chaos
quick_ideas: Map room use by hour for one week, so empty slots are visible
Choose one empty slot to fill, such as an adult class or studio hire, so the room earns.

workzap_build.text: dashboards_reports — A room and teacher calendar with self-booking, studio-hire slots and room-hour use measured.

problems.ask_first: Are weekday rooms empty all day, or only in the mornings?
problems.free_stops: How slots and pricing for hire are set up is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk through the school at the same weekday hours and on Saturday, so the empty rooms and crowded periods are easy to compare.
Give one person the job of offering quieter weekday slots when parents ask, so Saturday pressure eases during normal booking chats.

problems.words: Teachers' split causes arguments every month
quick_ideas: Write down each teacher's agreed split once, so there is one record
Show each teacher their lesson count before pay, so disagreements surface early.

workzap_build.text: Teacher pay worked out automatically from delivered lessons and agreed splits, with a monthly statement.

problems.ask_first: Do the arguments come from lesson counts, or from deductions like room costs?
problems.free_stops: The pay rules are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each teacher's own lesson tally with the office tally before pay time, so mismatches are caught before arguments start.
Keep one commission record in one notebook with one owner, so monthly pay talks rely on the same figures.

problems.words: Recital planning is all on WhatsApp and things get missed
quick_ideas: List every recital task with an owner and date once, so nothing is assumed
Confirm costume delivery dates with the tailor now, so late orders show early.

workzap_build.text: A recital planner with tasks, rehearsals, costume orders, seat counts and fees, with reminders sent automatically.

problems.ask_first: Is recital planning missed mostly on costumes, or on rehearsals and bookings?
problems.free_stops: The planner stages are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many recital jobs were mentioned in chat but never written on a list, so the weak handover point shows.
Keep one recital task page in the office and update it after each planning chat, so chat messages stop acting like the master list.

problems.words: Rental instruments come back damaged or not at all
quick_ideas: Number every rental instrument and note its condition once, so damage can be traced
List who has which instrument today by family reference, so missing ones show.

workzap_build.text: A rental register with condition notes, deposits and return reminders.

problems.ask_first: Do instruments more often come back damaged, or not come back at all?
problems.free_stops: How condition and deposits are tracked is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many rental instruments are out without a written return date, so you know the scale of loose tracking.
Make one staff member check returns against one notebook at handover time, so missing or damaged instruments are noticed the same day.

problems.words: Fees are late and chasing parents feels awkward
quick_ideas: Send reminders from the school's number, not the teacher's, so it isn't personal
Use one standard reminder for everyone, so no family feels singled out.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — Fee reminders sent automatically each term or month, with an overdue count for the office.

problems.ask_first: Do most families pay a little late, or do a few stay behind for months?
problems.free_stops: The reminder timing and wording are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many fee reminders go out after lessons have already happened, so you see where chasing is starting too late.
Set one regular time each week for fee follow-ups from the school side, so reminders feel routine instead of personal.

problems.words: People DM to book and we take a day to reply
quick_ideas: Put timings and how to book on one page you can share, so replies are quicker
Name one person to answer DMs at set times, so none wait overnight.

workzap_build.text: website_digital — Automatic WhatsApp replies with a booking link, and a booking page where parents choose slots.

problems.ask_first: Do DMs arrive mostly in the evening, or throughout the day?
problems.free_stops: The reply flow and booking page are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many booking messages arrive after teaching hours this week, so you can see when reply delays really start.
Keep one notebook by the phone for booking enquiries, so anyone on duty can reply without hunting through old chats.

never_say: Anything on music copyright or performance licensing, venue capacity or fire safety, or child-performer rules.
Consent-law advice on posting children's photos; pi only notes "need a parent-permission process".
Any idea that records learners' names, photos, recital videos, ages or exam results.
Promises of exam grades, or help with fake certificates or counterfeit instruments.
Any religious or cultural judgement about music or dance.
Business talk after an injury or event emergency; pi points to emergency services.

sample_reply.person: Make-up classes are driving us mad. Parents say lessons were missed and we have no way to check. What would you suggest?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, this is fixable, and the first steps are simple.
First, write one make-up rule and share it with parents, so every request is judged the same way.
Second, list the make-ups owed today, so you have a clean starting point.
The lasting fix would work by tracking every missed and make-up lesson under your rule and letting parents book make-ups themselves.

Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
